title: ChatGPT tells a Wolfforth, Texas, woman with a week-old spider bite, days of vomiting and a numb arm to go to the emergency room, where staff say that she should be there
summary: ChatGPT told Holli of Wolfforth, Texas, to go to the emergency room with a worsening spider bite; she says that staff there told her that the skin tissue was dying or dead.
account: Holli posts on TikTok as @hair.queen.holli from Wolfforth, Texas. She said that a spider had bitten her “a little over a week ago”. The bite was getting worse. She had vomited for days and could not keep water down. She woke with a numb arm. She asked ChatGPT whether she should go to the emergency room. It answered that her symptoms were “a ton of red flags” and that she should go immediately. At the emergency room, she said, staff told her “Yeah, you should be here”. They said that the skin tissue was dying or dead. Her video, recorded at the emergency room, was posted on 27 August 2025. The Express and the Daily Star retold it on 2 September 2025, and the Hindustan Times and The Economic Times on 3 September 2025. The hospital, diagnosis and treatment were not reported. No clinician has made a public statement. In a randomized study published in Nature Medicine on 9 February 2026, researchers at the University of Oxford and other institutions found that members of the public who used GPT-4o or two other chatbots chose the right level of care no more often than people who used their usual sources. The study does not concern Holli's case.
purpose: ChatGPT is a general-purpose conversational assistant. Answering a user's question, here whether to go to the emergency room, is its core function. OpenAI told the Mirror that its services “are not intended for use in the diagnosis or treatment of any health condition”. The Economic Times quoted it. The system gave triage advice and made no diagnosis.
segment: Consumer use of a general chatbot for triage advice

ratings.reason: Holli went to the emergency room after the chatbot told her to go. She says that staff told her that the bite's tissue was dying or dead. The diagnosis, treatment and outcome were not reported, so the benefit rated is the visit itself.

ai_role.statement: ChatGPT's contribution, on her account, was an unambiguous instruction to go immediately when she was unsure. The assessment and any treatment were the ER's. Whether earlier arrival changed her outcome is unknown. Everything traces to her TikTok, relayed by Reach plc tabloids and Indian lifestyle desks. Hindustan Times states that it “has not independently verified the claims”.

evidence.citation: Bean AM, Payne RE, Parsons G, et al., Reliability of LLMs as medical assistants for the general public: a randomized preregistered study, Nature Medicine 32(2):609-615, 9 February 2026. The authors work at the University of Oxford and other institutions, none of them at OpenAI, and they declare no competing interests. With 1,298 UK participants, they found that people who used GPT-4o, Llama 3 or Command R+ chose the right level of care no more often than people who used their usual sources.

fields.summary: ChatGPT told Holli of Wolfforth, Texas, to go to the emergency room with a worsening spider bite; she says that staff there told her that the skin tissue was dying or dead.
fields.account: Holli posts on TikTok as @hair.queen.holli from Wolfforth, Texas. She said that a spider had bitten her “a little over a week ago”. The bite was getting worse. She had vomited for days and could not keep water down. She woke with a numb arm. She asked ChatGPT whether she should go to the emergency room. It answered that her symptoms were “a ton of red flags” and that she should go immediately. At the emergency room, she said, staff told her “Yeah, you should be here”. They said that the skin tissue was dying or dead. Her video, recorded at the emergency room, was posted on 27 August 2025. The Express and the Daily Star retold it on 2 September 2025, and the Hindustan Times and The Economic Times on 3 September 2025. The hospital, diagnosis and treatment were not reported. No clinician has made a public statement. In a randomized study published in Nature Medicine on 9 February 2026, researchers at the University of Oxford and other institutions found that members of the public who used GPT-4o or two other chatbots chose the right level of care no more often than people who used their usual sources. The study does not concern Holli's case.

value.text: The chatbot recommended escalation. Holli chose to attend the ER, where clinicians examined her.

provenance.basis: Account: user acted on advice and ER staff assessed tissue damage.
